entities.name: Adrian Mung'andu
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Adrian Mung'andu (b. 1944) is a Zambian Catholic bishop who has served as Bishop of Chipata in eastern Zambia, one of the major dioceses in a country with one of Africa's highest proportions of baptised Catholics. Born in Zambia when it was still Northern Rhodesia, he was ordained a priest and rose to episcopal leadership as part of the first generation of Zambian bishops following independence in 1964.

Chipata diocese sits in Zambia's Eastern Province, bordering Malawi and Mozambique, a region with deep missionary roots from both British and White Father mission traditions. Mung'andu's episcopate engaged the pastoral challenges of a rural eastern African diocese: maintaining sacramental life across vast distances, building local seminary and catechetical infrastructure, addressing HIV/AIDS as it devastated communities from the 1980s onwards, and advocating for development and education.

His ministry represents the maturation of the Zambian Catholic Church from mission institution to self-governing local Church. Zambia's unusual status as one of the few African countries to have formally declared itself a Christian nation in 1991 placed its bishops in a unique public position—guardians of a constitutional Christian identity within a pluralist democratic framework. Mung'andu navigated this distinctive context throughout his episcopate.
